correctness.rationale: Exact \(B(n+t,5)\) norms yield \(Q_t(s)/(24(1-s)^6)\). The Cayley transform gives a quintic with first Routh column \(120\), \(120(2t+3)\), \(160(t+1)(t+2)\), \(8(2t+1)(2t+3)(2t+5)\), \(-64t(t-2)(t+1)(t+2)(t+3)(t+5)/((2t+1)(2t+5))\), and \(8(2t+3)p(t)\). Since \(p(t)=2[t(t+3)]^2-6t(t+3)-5\), its only positive zero is \(\tau\); Routh counts are exactly \(1,0,2\). Quartic Hurwitz determinants settle \(t=\tau\); exact factorization \(T_2(w)=120(w+3)(w^2+3)(w^2+4w+7)\) settles \(t=2\). Root reality and simplicity follow from conjugation and coefficient positivity. The checker reproduces algebra exactly and tests eight parameter choices; no finite-to-infinite inference is used.
